what goes to the memory MCP - locks it in, like alfred-navigation locks the navigation server

hooks.note: block force-push to main/master/develop

block recursive rm (Remove-Item -Recurse too) of /, ~, $HOME, a Windows drive, the cwd or its parent (. / ..), a bare *, or several top-level dirs at once; and a git discard, forced checkout/switch, stash drop/clear or reflog expire that would destroy work
block whole-file Read of a >200-line source file - locate via the navigation server first; caps cumulative half-split reconstruction
same gate on Bash: a bare `cat file.ts` of a large source file is the Read block routed through the shell

block a Read of a file that HOLDS a credential (content-judged: a JSON/dotenv key matching environment.json's secret_key_pattern with a live value) - presence only via `node guard-secret-value.js --presence <file> [KEY ...]`

same gate on Bash: cat/jq/grep/an inline node read of such a file, `echo $SECRET`, a bare `env`, or a credential-shaped literal in the command - a prose rule that failed live (a JSON.stringify(s.env) printed a token)

the THIRD read route: a Grep with output_mode content PRINTS the matching lines - measured live, a blocked Bash read of a settings.json was followed 8s later by a content Grep of the same path that returned its lines (count / files_with_matches modes print no value and pass)
block *-implementer dispatch without the docs-root flow/APPROVAL gate file (APPROVED/AUTO)
block a non-trivial git commit without the docs-root flow/COMMIT-GATE receipt (VERIFIED/WAIVED), and a git push / gh pr merge without flow/PUSH-GATE (ALFRED_CODE_PUSH_GATE=0 turns that half off)

Stop event: block a turn ending on a decision-shaped question in prose - re-emit as AskUserQuestion (measured stalls 13min-37h); also carries the fresh-session offer, past the window's absolute trigger, re-armed at 1.5x growth; and two log-only probes the analyzer counts - a done claim over a source edit (a file tool's or a shell write), unrun when nothing ran after it (ALFRED_CODE_DONE_GATE=0 off), and the first red build or test run of a streak; and a close dismissing a failure ('pre-existing', 'unrelated to my change', 'flaky') in a turn with a red run or a skipped test

SubagentStop: hold ONCE a subagent that stops on a wait nobody will end (a first-person 'I'll wait for...' close or its own ScheduleWakeup call) while it started no background work of its own - the parent's history is not its situation (field report: a fork dropped its whole brief this way)

PreToolUse AskUserQuestion: DENY once per ask text an ask whose own text breaks the house voice (an em- or en-dash, a double quote), carrying the corrected strings; INJECT the judgement notes, which land beside the user's answer and are worded for it - stale scope (an option naming repo/remote/job state with no fresh read this turn: verify before acting, re-ask if it moved), a recommendation contradicting an un-actioned earlier prompt, the fresh-session offer for the next ask, a live credential. Presence only

PostToolUseFailure: LOG-ONLY - the first red build or test run (npm / node --test / jest / vitest / pytest / dotnet / ng / go / cargo / mvn / gradle) of a failure streak writes one root-cause probe row with its tool_use_id, which analyze-usage.js --hook-blocks resolves against the transcript; nothing injected, never a block

PostToolUse: the same streak read from a run that exited 0 - a red runner summary behind a pipe is logged the same way; one streak per actor, ended when every run that went red in it is green again (or an hour with no red run)
PreToolUse Skill: block a deliberate orchestration run starting on another run's carried history past the window-scaled trigger - route it through an AskUserQuestion fresh-session choice

the same run invoked as a SLASH COMMAND emits no Skill event at all (measured: 4 of 4 runs slash-injected, zero Skill events in 45 messages) - UserPromptExpansion fires on that typed command and names it; the matcher (a regex with no colon, which the row format splits on) lists the orchestration commands under either spelling, so no ordinary prompt spawns the hook; it injects the ask, never blocks (a blocked expansion shows its reason to the user only)
the harness just auto-compacted, which proves the session hit its compaction point at a moment a Stop may never come - inject the fresh-session ask there too

before a compaction, write <docs-path>/flow/COMPACT-STATE - the live plan, the open flow stamps with their ages, the files this session wrote - with no model call; the compact SessionStart points at it

an EXISTING lint / format / analyzer config, or a strictness setting in tsconfig / MSBuild, cannot be changed to get a check green - creating one passes; the CONFIG-EDIT-ALLOW receipt honours a wanted change, ALFRED_CODE_CONFIG_PROTECT=0 turns it off
same gate on the shell routes (an in-place edit, redirect, tee, rm, mv or cp onto the config) - run inside shell-guards.js with the other shell guards
one session, one project: block a WRITE that lands outside the project root (reads/investigation untouched) - the change another repo needs is handed off as a task card
same gate on the shell routes (redirect, tee, in-place sed/perl, cp/mv, rm/mkdir/chmod, git -C, cd then a write) - run inside shell-guards.js

the desktop servers' process launchers, both routes' spellings: deny Windows-MCP App with mode launch_executable (any executable, caller-given args - the server excludes by tool name, never by mode) and every MacOS-MCP Shell call (a shell command no shell guard sees); App's launch / switch / resize pass; the DESKTOP-EXEC-ALLOW receipt (App, Shell, an executable, or *) honours a wanted launch

inject the answer budget (~3 sentences plus points) at the end of the turn's context - the short-answer rule mechanized; a correction turn writes one log-only probe row (ALFRED_CODE_CORRECTION_NUDGE=inject adds the memory-save line)
re-inject the budget after a COMPACTION rebuilds the context without it (measured absent for 277 of 366 messages in one session) - a startup/resume session gets it before the first prompt too
Stop event: block a wall-of-text answer (prose past the hard cap, no depth request in the user's message) - re-answer at budget
the architecture docs as the session's starting point: merged branches' doc versions folded into mainline, then ORIENTATION.md, this branch's overrides and how to read by section
the same orientation for a dispatched subagent - SessionStart context never reaches one, plus the snapshot the finish ask compares against
the finish ask, per agent: what THAT agent changed, once - the seat that made the change is the only context that knows why
doc reads recorded; the FIRST change under a source root held until a covering section was read, that section handed over inline
the same hold on the navigation server's two edit tools the stack keeps on (the other five are off at its launch) - the file is tool_input.relative_path; both routes' spellings

the same read record and hold on the shell routes - run inside shell-guards.js; every Bash|PowerShell|Monitor row of a guard shell-guards.js lists is wired as that ONE dispatcher (wiringRows), never on its own
once per session: a change that hit watch.json asks for the owning sections to be rewritten or confirmed
push a compact slice of shared memory (own project, cross-project preferences/corrections, related projects) into the session's starting context - engine memory.js copied beside it, not itself wired

a live monitor that never denies: the same call repeated 5 times with identical input, over 20 files written in one turn, the context at 80% of the fresh-session trigger - one row each, injected only when ALFRED_CODE_MONITOR=inject
a new turn: the monitor's per-turn counts reset
seeded OFF (ALFRED_CODE_TURN_CHECK=0): records each written path for the turn's one build check
the same record for the navigation server's two kept edit tools - the path is tool_input.relative_path, from the project root; both routes' spellings
the turn's ONE scoped tsc / dotnet build per root, first 20 error lines as a block, once per turn; timeout 60 on this Stop wiring alone, the one declared exception - its PostToolUse half keeps 10
what the last sessions on this branch did and ruled, injected at start (600 chars) - engine history.js copied beside it; ALFRED_CODE_HISTORY=0 off
records this session: commits, files left dirty, the user's AskUserQuestion answers - machine-local, <docs-path>/history/
wired env-gated: a plain node spawn that exits at its own env check unless ALFRED_CODE_INSTRUMENT=1 (seeded "0" in settings env - flip it for a measured run; see README)

plugins.note: inline Roslyn diagnostics on edit (complements the navigation server nav); needs csharp-ls (dotnet tool install -g csharp-ls); pin: the official marketplace entry's version - the package itself is empty, and the server is whatever csharp-ls is on PATH, unpinned
same for Angular/TS work; pin: the official marketplace entry's version - the server is whatever typescript-language-server is on PATH, unpinned

statusline HUD - optional since 2.2.0, recommended in every install (meta/recommendations.json always.plugins), at the scope the user picks for it (this project by default; a project-scope one gets its status line in the project's settings.local.json); pin: a third-party marketplace, its plugin.json version - auto-update is off there by default, so the stack's update is what moves it

mcps.name: alfred-navigation
mcps.args: -e SERENA_HOME=@SERENA_HOME@ -- node -e @ROOT_BOOT@ -- checkout uvx --python @UV_PYTHON@ @UV_EXCLUDE_FLAG@ @UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER@ --from serena-agent@SERENA_PIN@ serena start-mcp-server --context @SERENA_CONTEXT@ --enable-web-dashboard false @SERENA_PROJECT_FLAG@ @SERENA_PROJECT_DIR@
mcps.note: the navigation server (Serena): LSP symbol navigation; per-project SERENA_HOME (<data root>/serena/home - the data root ignores it, ~327MB LSP) isolates its registry/memories/logs/LSP, no pooling across projects/accounts; its home config points serena at <data root>/serena; --project-from-cwd self-activates the repo on launch (@SERENA_PROJECT_FLAG@ @SERENA_PROJECT_DIR@; a project with no .git whose serena folder moved under the data root registers --project . instead, which the cwd walk cannot find); PyPI (not git), dashboard off; --context names the stack's own serena context (@SERENA_CONTEXT@ = .claude/navigation-context.yml, copied there from stack/mcp) - the upstream claude-code one minus five editing tools and onboarding

mcps.name: browser
mcps.note: the browser server (Playwright MCP): drive a real browser for visual checks / web app verification - expanded after the selection into one browser-<engine> server per kept browser; --no-webmcp, so a visited page never adds tools of its own

mcps.name: alfred-memory
mcps.args: -e MCP_MEMORY_STORAGE_BACKEND=@MEMORY_BACKEND@ -e MCP_MEMORY_SQLITE_PATH=@MEMORY_DB_PATH@ -e MCP_MEMORY_SQLITE_PRAGMAS=busy_timeout=15000 -- node -e @ROOT_BOOT@ -- project uvx --python @UV_PYTHON@ @UV_EXCLUDE_FLAG@ @UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER@ --with numpy --from mcp-memory-service[sqlite]@MEMORY_PIN@ memory server
mcps.note: memory: required, like navigation and documentation (alfred-memory.md locks it in) - shared recall across sessions/projects; --memory-level picks where its db lives

mcps.name: alfred-documentation
mcps.note: the documentation server (Context7): up-to-date library/framework/SDK docs (beats recalled API knowledge) - the hosted server only since 2.0.0 (the local npx transport was cut, R32)

mcps.name: windows-desktop
mcps.args: -e WINDOWS_MCP_EXCLUDE_TOOLS=@WINDOWS_DESKTOP_EXCLUDE@ -e WINDOWS_MCP_TOOLS= -e ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false -- uvx --python @UV_PYTHON@ @UV_EXCLUDE_FLAG@ @UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER@ --from windows-mcp@WINDOWS_DESKTOP_PIN@ windows-mcp serve
mcps.note: the Windows desktop server (Windows-MCP): drives native Windows apps through UI Automation; Windows only, seeded for wpf / winforms there; opt-in (active: false - never in a no-selection run); PowerShell, Registry, Process and FileSystem off unless ALFRED_CODE_WINDOWS_DESKTOP_EXCLUDE says otherwise (WINDOWS_MCP_TOOLS registered empty, so an inherited one never overrides the list); App's launch_executable mode is denied by a house guard unless DESKTOP-EXEC-ALLOW allows it

mcps.name: macos-desktop
mcps.note: the macOS desktop server (MacOS-MCP): drives native macOS apps through the Accessibility API; macOS only, addable, seeded by no stack; opt-in (active: false); needs Accessibility and Screen Recording for the terminal and the uv-managed Python
